correctness.rationale: Using the Cai–Kiah–Nguyen–Yaakobi alternating-interval theorem for two distinct common one-deletion descendants, two equal-count Dyck parents differ on a unique even alternating interval of length 2k. Removing it leaves a Dyck word with a splice vertex at positive height; conversely both alternating phases can be inserted precisely at positive-height vertices. This gives an edge bijection without orientation ambiguity. Counting positive vertices H_m=(2m+1)C_m-C_{m+1} yields the edge sum. Every admissible even alternating interior interval yields one neighbor; there are at most (n-1)^2 such intervals, all realized by 1(10)^{n-1}0; for n>=3 alternating length-two intervals and positivity give uniqueness (for n=2 both maximize). Reversed Catalan-tail asymptotics yield |E|~(2/3)n C_n. Independent cross-enumeration checked 625 Dyck words, edge counts and short deletion intersection profiles; the theorem is not inferred from finite checks.
